counterfactual_missing_items: No acute abnormality of the pancreas
No history of fever, chills, previous similar pain, recent illness, abdominal trauma, alcohol, or illicit drug use
decisive_items: progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back
response.rationale: R5 is the strongest because the combination of back-radiating epigastric pain and markedly elevated lipase is diagnostic of acute pancreatitis even when early CT is normal. R6 explains epigastric pain and PPI failure but not the elevated lipase. R4 lacks ketosis/acidosis, while R1 and R3 are chronic or nonspecific and do not explain the acute presentation.

rejected.why: Known CKD and elevated creatinine are chronic comorbidities and do not explain acute epigastric pain or elevated lipase.
Decreased oral intake and diabetes are nonspecific; there is no evidence of malabsorption, steatorrhea, or chronic pancreatic insufficiency.
Hyperglycemia and diabetes history are present, but there are no ketones, acidosis, or typical DKA features, and it does not explain the lipase elevation or back-radiating pain.
